content:
Yes. **All 18 minimizations converged to the same final energy within numerical precision:**

\[
E_f \approx -48992.8206000178\ \text{eV}.
\]

Across the recorded results, the largest visible difference is only about

\[
1.1\times10^{-10}\ \text{eV}
\]

for the entire 11,052-atom cell—effectively roundoff noise. For example:

- Step 6: \(-48992.82060001776\) eV  
- Step 10: \(-48992.82060001778\) eV  
- Step 33: \(-48992.82060001781\) eV  
- Step 60: \(-48992.82060001777\) eV  
- Step 70: \(-48992.82060001776\) eV  

Thus, although the unloading configurations began with slightly different energies, unconstrained zero-load relaxation brought all of them into the same energy minimum to numerical accuracy. This strongly suggests that the selected unloading stress-drop states belong to the same relaxed basin under the fixed-box, all-atoms-free conditions—not 18 distinct metastable minima. Equality of energy alone does not prove atom-by-atom identity, but the displacement fields should be interpreted in that context.
